title: The Oath of the Ninefold Court
premise: When the border wards of Vhalen collapse and the stars go dark, temple scribe Jonah Kavanagh discovers the charms they have secretly sold for twelve years were fragments of a dying covenant — the Ninefold Court's oath that binds the realm together. The 'king' on the throne is now the Hollow Regent, a crown-born hunger wearing the monarch's face, feeding on dragon-fire to unmake the law itself. Jonah, whose debt-bound blood marks them as the last heir of the Court's ninth seat, must gather the scattered oath-keepers, relight the last dragon's heart-flame, and speak the broken vow aloud. In the end Jonah refuses the throne offered to them, instead dissolving the Court into a freely sworn compact — justice chosen, not inherited — as the stars return.
about_author: Emrys Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-scrolls before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people bound by systems older than themselves, from a drafty study full of unlabeled keys.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Jonah Kavanagh, POV. A night in the Scriptorium of Saint Verre: Jonah copies wards by day, sells illegal charms by night, counting down a twelve-year debt to the temple. When a customer pays with an old coin stamped with nine interlocked rings, Jonah feels their own charms hum in answer. Beat: restless unease — a life built on small transgressions about to crack open.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. At midnight every star in the sky goes out at once; the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass heard through stone. Panic floods the city of Vhalen. From the scriptorium tower Jonah watches the darkness roll in like a tide, and the coin in their pocket burns cold. Beat: awe curdling into dread as the ordinary world ends.

chapters.title: What the Temple Owes
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The High Cantor reveals the truth: the temple has known the wards were failing for years, and Jonah's 'debt' was never money — it was service to a hidden order of oath-keepers. Jonah is named, absurdly, as heir to the Ninth Seat of the Ninefold Court. Beat: betrayal and vertigo; the life Jonah thought they chose was assigned all along.

chapters.title: The Hollow Regent
chapters.summary: Sera Ilvane, a disgraced ward-knight, POV. In the palace, Sera glimpses what sits behind the king's eyes during an audience — something vast and patient wearing her sovereign like a glove. She flees with proof: a royal seal that weeps black wax. Beat: horror and guilt; she once swore the oath that let the thing in.

chapters.title: Nine Rings, Broken
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Fleeing the temple as the Regent's inquisitors burn it, Jonah meets Sera on the road. Comparing the coin and the seal, they learn the Court had nine seats, eight abandoned or dead — and the Ninth's heir was hidden in plain sight as a debtor. Beat: reluctant alliance between two people who each failed their oaths differently.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Market
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. In the smugglers' warren of Lowcandle, Jonah seeks old customers — the poor, the desperate, the marked — who unknowingly hold fragments of the covenant in the charms they bought. Some give them up; one man dies protecting his daughter's charm. Beat: grief and responsibility; Jonah sees the human cost of everything they sold.

chapters.title: A Dragon, Mostly Ash
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Beneath the Cinderfell mountains lives Vaskarath, the last dragon, kept alive by a guttering heart-flame no bigger than a candle. Ancient and bitter, he names the price of his aid: someone must carry the flame to the First Hearth, and carriers always burn. Beat: grim wonder; hope introduced with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: The Fourth Seat Refuses
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The Fourth Seat, Magister Ondrey, alive and comfortable in a university tower, refuses to help — the Court's justice failed him once, and he will not be bound again. His refusal teaches Jonah the theme's sharp edge: oaths imposed are cages. Beat: frustration giving way to uncomfortable self-recognition.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Ford
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Ambushed crossing the Greywater, Sera holds the ford alone while Jonah escapes with the charm-fragments. Captured, she faces the Regent's questioners — and her former oath-brother among them. Beat: sacrifice and shame; loyalty tested against the memory of what she broke.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Guided by dreams sent through the dying covenant, Jonah walks the dream-court of the Ninefold Throne and speaks briefly with the king still buried inside the Regent — a man aware, imprisoned, whispering 'finish it.' Beat: pity for the enemy; the monster is also a victim, complicating Jonah's resolve.

chapters.title: Lowcandle Rises
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The Regent outlaws magic-holders outright; soldiers sweep Lowcandle. Jonah's old customers — the debtors, the marked, the forgotten — form an unlikely militia around the fragments. Belonging, not blood, becomes their armor. Beat: defiant warmth; the first time Jonah leads rather than hides.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Questioning House
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Imprisoned and interrogated, Sera turns her questioner — her oath-brother Dain — by showing him the weeping seal and what he's truly serving. Together they break out, but Dain stays behind to hold the door. Beat: redemption purchased at cost; forgiveness neither earned nor refused.

chapters.title: The Second Hearth
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The company reaches the First Hearth's antechamber and finds it sealed by a riddle of inheritance: only one who owes and is owed may enter. Jonah's debt-marked blood opens it — the first time their bondage has ever been a gift. Beat: bittersweet revelation; the chain and the key are the same metal.

chapters.title: Ondrey's Return
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Magister Ondrey arrives uninvited, having watched Lowcandle's stand and changed his mind — not for the Court, but for the people who chose each other without one. He brings the missing Third Seat fragment and a warning: the Regent marches on the Hearth. Beat: cautious reconciliation; justice rebuilt from refusal.

chapters.title: The March of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. The Regent's army — hollow-eyed conscripts with extinguished reflections — descends. The defenders prepare a doomed stand at the Hearth's gates while Vaskarath readies the heart-flame for carrying. Jonah volunteers to bear the flame, hiding that carriers burn. Beat: quiet terror beneath resolve; a lie told to protect others.

chapters.title: Fire Against Hunger
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. The battle at the gates: charm-bearers ignite their fragments into a wall of light, Ondrey duels the Regent's herald, and Sera holds the line where Dain died. The Hollow advance falters before flame that remembers its oaths. Beat: ferocious courage; ordinary people burning brighter than knights.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Inside the Hearth, bearing the dragon-flame, Jonah begins to burn — and understands why carriers die. But the flame responds to willing vows, not suffering: by speaking their own true oath aloud, Jonah feeds it choice instead of flesh. Beat: transcendence through honesty; the fire wants consent, not sacrifice.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Climax. At the Ninefold Throne, Jonah confronts the Hollow Regent with the relit flame and the assembled fragments. Speaking the restored oath, they call the buried king's name; the crown-thing is unmade not by force but by being witnessed, named, and refused. The king dies free, human, grateful. Beat: catharsis; the monster defeated by acknowledgment, not annihilation.

chapters.title: An Empty Throne Offered
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. With the Regent fallen, the surviving seats and the assembled people turn to Jonah — Ninth Seat, flame-bearer, heir. The old law demands they take the throne and reforge the Court as it was. Beat: the temptation of rightful power; everything Jonah suffered seems to demand they inherit it.

chapters.title: The Tenth Voice
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Jonah refuses the throne and instead proposes a tenth voice: a compact sworn freely by every seat, settlement, and stranger — justice renewed annually by consent, dissolvable by the same. The dragon Vaskarath witnesses it with the last of his flame, then finally lets go. Beat: thematic resolution; belonging chosen over inheritance.

chapters.title: Stars Over Vhalen
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. Weeks later: the stars return one by one over a city rebuilding without a king. Sera takes up ward-work under the new compact; Ondrey teaches oath-law to anyone who comes. The temple's debt-ledgers are burned in celebration. Beat: tender renewal; institutions remade as promises between equals.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Last Stall
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Epilogue. Jonah keeps a small market stall in Lowcandle — not selling charms now, but teaching anyone who wishes to write their own. A child asks if the stories about the Ninth Seat are true. Jonah says the seat was real; the story is still being written. Beat: warm closure; legacy passed as invitation, not obligation.
